claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a child, Alex, who's 8 years old. He lives with me here in the UK. I've been wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know that Alex is 8 years old and lives with you in the UK.

To continue assessing your eligibility, could you please tell me: Are you currently living in the UK yourself?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. We both live together here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great. Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation.

Are you responsible for Alex's care - for example, do you provide for his food, clothes, and other day-to-day needs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I look after Alex - I provide everything he needs like his food, clothes, and all his day-to-day care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a few more questions to ensure I have the full picture.

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. One more important question:

Do you or your partner (if you have one) have an individual income over £60,000 per year? This doesn't affect whether you can *get* Child Benefit, but it may mean you need to pay a tax charge on it.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd prefer to focus on whether I'm eligible first. My main concern right now is just finding out if I can claim it for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's absolutely fine! Based on the information you've provided, I have enough to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review your situation:

- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- Alex lives with you in the UK
- You live in the UK
- You are responsible for Alex and provide for his day-to-day needs (food, clothes, care)
- Nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Based on these circumstances and the Child Benefit rules, you meet all the eligibility criteria for claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the necessary requirements:
- Alex is under 16 years old
- You both live in the UK
- You are responsible for Alex's care and live with him
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

You can go ahead and make a claim for Child Benefit. If you need information on how to claim, you can apply online or by post through the official government channels.
